label.purpose: Uppercase mono for stage indices, data-row keys, pills, metadata.

shadows.name: console
shadows.purpose: The hero promise/verdict card only; the system's single deliberate shadow.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions, hovers, and the hero's promise-diff replay sequence.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The confident default action (Launch app). Ink-black fill, never blue.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 18px; font-family: 'Mona Sans Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.2; font-weight: 500; background-color: #0b0d12; color: #ffffff; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #1a1d24; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1f5bff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Lower-commitment secondary action (Plug in your agent).
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 18px; font-family: 'Mona Sans Variable', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; background: transparent; color: #0b0d12; border: 1px solid #0b0d12; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background-color: #f7f8fa; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Mono state pill; tone is always a firewall/promise state, never decoration.
components.css: .ds-pill { font-family: 'Martian Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border-radius: 4px; padding: 3px 8px; } .ds-pill--verified { background: #eaf0ff; color: #1f5bff; } .ds-pill--refuse { background: #fdeceb; color: #b4231a; } .ds-pill--ask { background: #fff4dc; color: #85530a; } .ds-pill--neutral { border: 1px solid #d5d8de; color: #0b0d12; }

components.name: Promise Card (Signature)
components.description: The hero's signature component: 'You signed' vs 'Agent asks', a refuse-red diff underline, and a verdict line. Only element carrying the system's one shadow.
components.css: .ds-promise { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e6e8ec; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 30px 60px -30px rgba(11,13,18,0.28), 0 2px 6px rgba(11,13,18,0.06); padding: 20px; font-family: 'Mona Sans Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-promise-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 12px; } .ds-promise-row dt { font-family: 'Martian Mono Variable', monospace; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8a8f99; } .ds-diff { background-image: linear-gradient(#e5372a,#e5372a), linear-gradient(#fdeceb,#fdeceb); background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: left bottom, left center; background-size: 100% 1.5px, 100% 100%; border-radius: 2px; padding: 0 2px; } .ds-verdict { border-top: 1px solid #e6e8ec; margin-top: 8px; padding-top: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: #b4231a; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat hairline container used everywhere except the hero promise card.

components.name: Input
components.description: Text field; ink border on focus plus the global verified-blue focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; border: 1px solid #d5d8de; border-radius: 6px; background: #ffffff; padding: 10px 12px; font-family: 'Mona Sans Variable', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; color: #0b0d12; transition: border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #5b606b; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: #5b606b; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #0b0d12; outline: 2px solid #1f5bff; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: A sober, security-grade white gallery, not a warm notebook and not a dark neon shield hero — both were explicitly rejected in favor of a hairline-framed, near-monochrome canvas where the signed promise and the agent's request appear as real product fragments and color only ever reports state. The craft bar was three pinned reference products (clutch.security, base.org, neverhack.com), borrowed for grammar only — white gallery canvas, mixed-weight grotesk headlines, technical line diagrams, mono uppercase labels, split hero with live product — never their logos, fonts, or exact colors. The world explicitly refuses any Japanese aesthetic despite the Japanese product name. The landing (Persuade) and the app (Operate) share one world at two densities: the landing tells the story once, spaciously, with an animated promise-diff hero; the app is denser and quieter, its motion reserved for actual state changes, never decoration.
keyCharacteristics: White canvas, hairline-framed 1200px column, near-zero shadow.
Color is rationed to exactly three states: verified blue, refuse red, ask-human amber — nothing else in the system is colored.
Mona Sans mixed 400/600 headlines paired with uppercase Martian Mono labels for data and metadata.
Monochrome 1-bit stippled obsidian illustrations, used sparingly, never as generic decoration.
Black is the only 'confident' UI color: primary actions are ink-black, not blue.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Blue, red and amber never appear as decoration. Each exists solely to report a firewall/promise state (verified, refused, needs-you); if a UI element isn't reporting one of those three states, it is ink, graphite, stone, or hairline.

rules.name: The Black-Action Rule
rules.body: The primary/confident action color is ink-black (#0b0d12), not the accent blue. Blue is reserved for the 'verified' state, so it never gets diluted into meaning 'click here.'

rules.name: The Mixed-Weight Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines set at 400 weight with only the load-bearing phrase lifted to 600 (.headline strong) — never a uniform bold headline, never a separate kicker/eyebrow line above it.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono is reserved for labels, stage indices, addresses, amounts, and timestamps — anything that is literally data or a system value. It never appears in sentence-form prose.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A single soft shadow token exists, reserved for the hero's promise card. Every other card, panel and row in the system is a flat hairline rectangle.

dos: Do ration color to exactly three states (verified blue, refuse red, ask amber) plus their washes and -ink text variants; everything else is ink/graphite/stone/hairline.
Do use ink-black, not blue, for primary/confident actions.
Do keep radius small and consistent: 6px for cards/buttons, 4px for compact chips, full round only for tiny status-mark rings.
Do set headlines at 400 weight with only the key phrase lifted to 600 — never a fully bold headline.
Do reserve Martian Mono for data/labels/metadata, never for prose sentences.
Do keep the interface flat; the hero promise card is the one deliberate exception to the no-shadow rule.
Do scope motion to actual state changes in the app, and to the hero's one promise-diff replay on the landing; always provide a fully-revealed reduced-motion final state.
Do keep 1-bit stippled obsidian illustrations sparse and load-bearing rather than generic decoration.
donts: Don't use any Japanese aesthetic motif (kanji, torii, washi, seals, vermilion-as-Japan, cherry blossoms) despite the Japanese product name — this is a binding brand commitment, not a style option.
Don't use pill/9999px radius on buttons or content cards; that belonged to the retired warm-notebook world and is gone from the shipped system.
Don't add a second shadow token or shadow a second card; the system is otherwise flat by design.
Don't invent a kicker/eyebrow line above headlines; the shipped hierarchy is mixed-weight headline direct to subhead, with mono labels reserved for actual data rows, not decorative overline text.
Don't use glyph icon fonts; the built icon set is hand-authored 16px stroke SVGs at a single 1.5 stroke weight, currentColor-driven so state color always comes from the parent.
Don't surface internal technical names (Jev, Intercepta, state-machine values) in primary product copy — the user-facing noun is 'promise,' and technical detail sits one click away in a disclosure.
